newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow bank to buy 20 pct of Russian Troika Dialog.
newsitem.headline: Moscow bank to buy 20 pct of Russian Troika Dialog.

text.p: Moscow's municipally owned Bank Moskvy said on Friday it would buy about 20 percent of Russian investment bank Troika Dialog.

The move is the latest stage in a consolidation in which leading investment banks and brokerages are seeking Russian or foreign banking partners with stronger financial muscle as Russian securities markets expand.
"It is planned that Bank Moskvy will buy a bit less than 20 percent of Troika Dialog," Bank Moskvy President Andrei Borodin told a news conference.
He declined to say how much his bank would pay for the shares or where the stock would come from.
He said that he had been offered the chairmanship of Troika Dialog's five-member board, currently held by Peter Derby, who set up the bank.
Troika Dialog, one of the leading operators on the Russian share market, has for some time been the only large institution which had not formed an alliance with another company.
But Troika may continue looking for other partners after the deal with Bank Moskvy is completed.

"As we go, we will view our strategic position from time to time and if that facilitates any additional domestic or foreign cooperation, we would be open to looking at that as time and other considerations permit," Derby said.
Russian and foreign brokerages, trying not to lose their positions on the rapidly growing market, have recently announced a string of mergers and unions.
"The stock market is growing very quickly," Troika Dialog President Ruben Vardanyan said.
"To keep a position on the market you have to get stronger at a rate which is not allowed simply at the expense of profit, you need consolidation with a partner."

Last month one of Russia's biggest banks in terms of assets, the International Company for Finance and Investment (ICFI, or Bank MFK in Russian), announced a merger with Renaissance Capital investment bank.
SBC Warburg said it would set up a Russian banking joint venture with Brunswick Investments Ltd.
Last year Austria's bank Creditanstalt and Moscow brokerage Grant formed a 50/50 joint venture.
Borodin said one of the areas of interest of the new alliance would be privatisation in the City of Moscow.
"It is one of the fields of our mutual activity," he said.
The City of Moscow owns 60 percent of Bank Moskvy and banks and companies the rest.
